facts.fact: The Ministry of ICT and National Guidance published the Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040 in September 2022 with a foreword by President Museveni; its text says the Vision 'has been put in place' (verb: put in place; no adopting act or cabinet approval of the Vision itself is stated, though it assigns Cabinet the role of approving policies).

The Vision sets a 2040 horizon with targets for 2025, 2030 and 2040, a mid-term evaluation in FY2028/29 and a final evaluation in FY2039/40, so it is inside its stated period; it also calls itself an 'overarching 8-year ICT development framework' and a living document. Text public: yes.

The Vision carries a financing table and a cost implementation matrix (Annex 2) putting first-phase financing to 2030 at UGX 6.08 trillion (UGX 6,084,250,000 thousand), by pillar, with a results framework matrix of indicators and 2030 targets in Annex 1.

The Vision names the Digital Transformation Program Working Group (heads of MDAs under the NDP III Digital Transformation Program) to coordinate implementation, prepare costed action plans and quarterly, semi-annual and annual implementation reports and run annual performance reviews, with technical working groups under it and the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance leading.

The Vision lists national budget appropriations to MDAs and local governments, concessional loans and grants, Uganda Development Bank pre-financing, private equity and domestic revenue mobilisation as financing measures, and says the Digital Transformation Program 'faces limited resource allocation from the national budget'; it ties no budget line or allocation to the Vision.
